census.internal_tail_jumps_note: all three are landing-pad jumps to the separate-FDE cleanup fragment at 0x5d50a06
census.relative_note: four R_X86_64_RELATIVE records whose addend is the routine address; the routine is reached only through them
census.stored_qwords_note: raw 8-byte scan hits inside .rela.dyn at the addend positions of the four RELATIVE records above, not separate stored pointers

entries.stage: delete the qword at inherited-rbp +0x08 if non-null, then resume
teardown inherited-r13 temp, release inherited-r12, then resume
teardown inherited-r15 temp, teardown inherited-r13 temp, release inherited-r12, then resume

cleanup_fragment.note: a separate FDE entered only via the routine's landing-pad jumps; the register roles are stated as inherited, not as named objects

counter.rule: non-zero at entry: increment once and skip the refresh sequence; zero at entry: build temps, refresh the pointer only if the counter still reads 0, then increment once

dispose.rule: null pointer skipped; vtable slot +0x08 equal to 0x5d486c0: delete with size 0x10; otherwise call the slot value with the pointer

exit.note: calls pthread_mutex_unlock on its argument; only the argument and the call are pinned

merge.order: temp2 merge (flag-gated) before temp1 merge; teardowns temp2 then temp1

not_claimed: what the source, the destination, or any field denotes
the third argument of the +0x318 call (rdx is set to 0 before the +0x300 call but may be clobbered by it)
which source-level object the cleanup fragment's inherited-rbp +0x08 denotes
the exact call-range to landing-pad mapping in the LSDA (only the three entries and their targets are pinned)
caller semantics (there are no direct call sites)
behaviour on dangling pointers or a null destination or source (the model raises)
the exception path beyond the cleanup fragment's staged actions

produce.disposal: delete[] the qword at temp +0x08 when non-null

refresh_pointer.effect: the new pointer it writes into the out slot replaces source +0x1930; the out slot is then zeroed and disposed of again (a no-op)

teardown.note: called on temp2 then temp1; a freshly initialized temp tears down to nothing (its +0x50 flag byte is 0, its +0x70/+0x80 pointers null)

trailing_bytes: bytes from 0x5d50dc5 to 0x5d50dd0 are int3 padding, not part of the routine
